newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss decline offer to send "mad cows" to Nepal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss decline offer to send "mad cows" to Nepal.

text.p: Switzerland has politely declined a Nepal-based Hindu group's offer to provide a home in the Himalayas for 230,000 cattle due to be slaughtered in a Swiss "mad cow" cull, a government official said on Tuesday.
A spokesman for the Federal Veterinary Office in Berne cited concerns about cruelty to animals as the main reason for killing them in Switzerland rather than shipping them abroad.
"You cannot ship 230,000 cows by air," he told Reuters, adding that exporting the animals also threatened to spread the brain-wasting disease.

The World Hindu Federation had urged Berne to cancel the cull, which aims to wipe out bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) in Switzerland. Some scientists believe BSE can be passed to humans. Switzerland trails only Britain in total BSE cases.
Hindus worship cows and revere them. "For us slaughtering cow is more crime than slaughtering anything," the group wrote to Swiss leaders.

The Federation had suggested the Swiss government give it the $257 million envisioned for the cull. It wrote: "Please let us know if we can take these cows in Nepal and Swiss government will pay us $257 million to maintain the cows for well?"
